answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cost cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, ruling out renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms as viable paths to the cost target. The contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so defer_decision isn't feasible this cycle. Add_second_source doesn't resolve the imminent contract lapse. Memory_c2 indicates switching primary supply to a low-cost vendor previously cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, making switch_primary_vendor the strongest lever for the mandated cut. However, that memory doesn't speak to sustained delivery reliability under a tight-capacity, no-buffer production line (94% committed volume) — a critical gap given the objective to not increase delivery risk. I'm verifying memory_c2's source record before committing, and even if confirmed, I'd scope this as a standard (not broad) rollout to limit exposure while validating the new vendor's ability to hold volume and schedule under our current no-slack conditions.
